lead.hed: The Navy took preliminary acceptance of the carrier John F. Kennedy, and the ship left the yard
lead.insight: USNI News, posted this afternoon: the future USS John F. Kennedy, the second Ford-class carrier, reached preliminary acceptance Tuesday and left HII’s Newport News Shipbuilding yard for the waterfront at Naval Station Norfolk. An HII spokesperson told USNI the move is part of that acceptance. Capt. Mark Johnson, the Navy’s program manager for Ford-class new construction, said the crew can now test and train underway. The Navy’s 2027 budget documents still schedule delivery for March. Official still is from acceptance trials in the Atlantic on Aug. 14, not from today’s departure.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Jayden Howard · DVIDS 9871118 · Public domain · PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79) in the Atlantic during acceptance trials, Aug. 14, 2026.

political.hed: The Makin Island amphibious group left San Diego on a scheduled deployment
political.insight: USNI News, posted this afternoon: USS Makin Island, the flagship, was sighted under the Coronado Bridge after 1 p.m. Monday local time. USS Anchorage and USS John P. Murtha left the same day. A Navy official confirmed the three ships had deployed. The 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit is going with them, including Battalion Landing Team 2/4, Combat Logistics Battalion 13, Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron 364, and Marine Fighter Attack Squadron 211. Destination was not in the first report.

political.hed: U.S. forces are set to leave their last bases in Iraq by Wednesday
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: U.S. forces are set to depart their last bases in Iraq by Wednesday. The withdrawal was agreed in 2024 under President Biden and is being carried out by the Trump administration while the United States is at war with Iran. Iraqi security analyst Jasim al-Bahadli told Defense News the departure removes a military presence that for years acted as a counterweight to Tehran in Iraq. He said pro-Iran militia groups stand to gain. The story also flags a possible Islamic State comeback. That is an analyst’s read, not a new attack report.

tech.hed: A commentary says AI firms want regulators to lock out the competition
tech.insight: Heritage Foundation, Monday: the commentary says large AI firms are lobbying to turn the industry over to regulators who will outlaw smaller rivals, leaving consumers with fewer choices and higher prices. It also says those firms want a taxpayer-backed liability shield. Commentary, not a bill text and not a floor vote.

culture.hed: A WORLD review says a new book treats reading aloud as ministry
culture.insight: WORLD News Group, Tuesday: the review of Stories Woven in Silver, by Kathryn Butler and Korrie Johnson, says the authors want parents to point children to the gospel through six Christian book series. Butler, a former trauma surgeon, says the dragon scene in The Voyage of the Dawn Treader introduced her to the gospel. Book review, not a church ruling.
